svg.aria-label: Belly band sizing: flat length equals twice the piece width plus twice the stack thickness plus half inch glue overlap plus eighth inch ease; band height tracks product size; soap bar example resolves to 9.625 inches

g.text: How a band is sized
Two measurements define a band, and both come from the product it wraps — circumference and height
flat length = (2 × piece width) + (2 × stack thickness) + ½″ glue overlap + ⅛″ ease
Worked example — soap bar 3.5 × 2.25 × 1″
band height 1.5″ (¼ of piece height)
glue seam on the back, centred — the front panel stays unbroken
Ease adjusts, height tracks size
· slip-on fits: ease up to ¼″
· soft stacks (folded textiles, towels): ease drops to zero
· “A band cut short does not close, and there is no fixing it after the fact.”
Published height guidance splits by product size:
· 1″ for small products — cosmetics, jewelry (MyBoxPrinter)
· 1–3″ band range; 2–3″ for books and apparel (MyBoxPrinter)
· 3–4″ ideal band width (ChinaPrinting4U)
· ≈¼ of the piece height on stationery examples, 1.25–2.5″ (4OVER4)
Read together: small products run narrow, books and boxes run
wide — enough for a logo, a copy line and a barcode — with the
20–30% coverage ceiling as the ceiling test.
Artwork: ≈3 mm bleed on all sides (4OVER4 cross-checks at ⅛″), key elements inside a 5 mm safe zone, images at 300 DPI, PDF submission — every edge of a wrapped band is a trim edge.
